column1: # The flash layout
column2: and the reason it is committed rather than left to espflash.

column1: # espflash's default table has one `factory` app slot and no `otadata`
# is enough to run the box and not enough to update it: OTA needs somewhere to
# write the next image while the current one is still running
# record which of the two the bootloader should pick.
# This is the stock layout with the smallest change that makes room for
# `otadata`. `phy_init` keeps its offset and the app still starts at 0x10000
# so the only partition that moves at all is `nvs`
# is the standard ESP-IDF OTA table — 0x4000 of `nvs`
# and it is standard precisely because `otadata` has to come out of the 0x7000
# bytes between the partition table and the app
# `nvs` here holds Wi-Fi calibration and nothing of ours; 16 KB is what every
# ESP-IDF OTA project ships with.
# The chip is 8 MB
column2: measured 2026-09-16 from espflash's connection banner and

column1: # confirmed by the second-stage bootloader's own `SPI Flash Size : 8MB`. At
# 8 MB the sizing question stops being interesting: 3 MB a slot against an
# image of 1
column3: 128 bytes is 2.8x headroom. A slot the image outgrows is a

column1: # build-time failure — espflash refuses it — not a runtime one.
# There is deliberately no `factory` slot. espflash writes `ota_0` directly
# third copy would cost space for recovery value that shorting J100 already
# covers
column2: and its presence changes which partition the bootloader prefers.

column1: # `otadata` could instead have gone above `ota_1`
# It is not there because every reference table in ESP-IDF puts it at 0xd000
# and the boot path is the wrong place to be the first to try something else.
